media.alt: The Science of Early Child Development: Collaborating Across Continents

content.text: What could 4 faculty members, 79 students in two trans-continental universities, have in common?

They are all facilitators and participants in a Science of Early Child Development course delivered across Aga Khan University and University of Toronto campuses in Canada, Pakistan, Tanzania and Uganda. Taught by four faculty members - one from each country - the SECD course provided a platform to learn about child development and share early childhood development practices across three continents.

The sessions brought together students from various academic disciplines, from fourth year biology students at the University of Toronto, second year undergraduate nursing students in Kampala and Dar es Salaam and IED early child development practitioners teaching in schools in Karachi from AKU. For six weeks of the 18-week course, they learnt and shared experiences about early human development with their peers using a blended and digital learning approach.

Feedback from participants on their learning outcomes were very positive and the participation of students from different countries and continents advanced understanding about diverse cultural practices and norms around child development. This learning method was immensely successful allowing collaboration between various institutions and displaying the relevance of using such methods in future courses..

Reacting to the BDL methodology, one participant said, "I had a good time and enjoyed the many discussions that I had with the fellow students in my group. The interactive discussions on 'Problem Based Learning' and the way everyone shared material with each other and related examples from their home countries made the content even more relevant."

The students were also excited to apply theory to practice as illustrated by another student who said "I have secured a place to develop an ECD centre in my home village. I will be helping my community by involving them in the upbringing of their children and will provide information about early childhood development".
The planning phase was the most challenging. However, with guidance from the faculty, the BDL team, mentor and subject experts, it was a huge success.

The course was part of a capacity building programme for faculty and other key stakeholders in ECD and was conducted in partnership with AKU's Institute for Human Development and the University of Toronto's Fraser Mustard Institute for Human Development, with technical support from the Aga Khan Foundation Geneva and Red River College in Manitoba, Canada. The programme is a sub-project of the 'Institutional Partnerships for Human Development' under the 'Partnership for Advancing Human Development in Africa and Asia', jointly funded by the Government of Canada through the Department of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development and AKF Canada.
